name: deskyard
description: Use a Deskyard desktop (a Linux desktop with a shared Chromium) from inside it or remotely through its agent API. Run commands as `deskyard [-d NAME] <name> <arguments...>`; arguments are positional in the listed order, flags go after the command name.

globalFlags.name: --desktop
globalFlags.description: use the remote NAME (see `deskyard remote list`); before the command

environment.name: DESKYARD_REMOTE
environment.description: remote to use when -d isn't given

environment.name: DESKYARD_URL
environment.description: desktop URL (https://host/alice) to use without a remotes.json; needs DESKYARD_TOKEN

environment.name: DESKYARD_TOKEN
environment.description: agent token for DESKYARD_URL, and the default for `remote add --token`

environment.name: DESKYARD_SETTLE
environment.description: seconds screenshot and zoom wait before capturing (default 0.3)

exitCodes.meaning: error (the message on stderr says what to do next)
usage error (bad command, flag or argument)
exec, shell and screen actions pass through the exit code of the command on the desktop

commands.name: screenshot
commands.description: Takes a PNG screenshot of the whole screen, after a short settle delay (DESKYARD_SETTLE seconds, default 0.3) so the screen reflects your last action. Without FILE, or with -, the PNG goes to stdout. Take one before acting and after, to see what happened; coordinates in the image are screen coordinates.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: where to write the PNG on this machine; - or omitted for stdout

output.description: PNG image bytes on stdout, or nothing when FILE is given (the file is written on this machine)

commands.where: inside a desktop it acts locally; elsewhere on the chosen remote (-d NAME)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error; otherwise the exit code of the action on the desktop

commands.name: zoom
commands.summary: PNG of a region at full resolution
commands.description: Takes a PNG of just the region from the top-left corner X0 Y0 to the bottom-right corner X1 Y1 (exclusive), at full resolution: use it to read small text or check details. X1 must be greater than X0 and Y1 greater than Y0.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: where to write the PNG on this machine; - or omitted for stdout

output.description: PNG image bytes on stdout, or nothing when FILE is given (the file is written on this machine)

commands.name: exec
commands.summary: run a command on the desktop
commands.description: Runs one command as user (in /workspace unless --cwd) and streams its stdin, stdout and stderr; exits with the command's exit code. The command is run as given, not through a shell: for pipes, globs or && use `-- bash -lc '...'`.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: buffer the output and print one JSON object {"stdout","stderr","exit"} instead of streaming; exit 0 when the JSON was printed

flags.name: --tty
flags.description: run in a terminal (for programs that need one); stdout and stderr are merged

output.description: the command's stdout and stderr as they arrive; with --json one object {"stdout":string,"stderr":string,"exit":int}, using "stdoutBase64"/"stderrBase64" (base64) instead when the output isn't UTF-8

fields.stderrBase64: standard error, base64, when not UTF-8
fields.stdoutBase64: standard output, base64, when not UTF-8

examples: deskyard exec --json -- bash -lc 'cd app && npm test'
commands.where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the command's own exit code; 1 when it couldn't run (connection, token, stopped desktop), 2 usage error

commands.name: shell
commands.description: Opens an interactive bash login shell on the desktop in your terminal (raw mode, resizes follow your window). Exit with `exit` or Ctrl-D. For scripted use, prefer exec.
commands.where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the shell's exit code; 1 when it couldn't start

commands.name: cp
commands.summary: copy files to or from a desktop
commands.description: Copies a file or directory between this machine and a desktop; write the desktop side as NAME:/path (NAME is a remote; an empty NAME, as in :/path, means the chosen remote). A file lands at DST, or inside DST when it is an existing directory. A directory's contents land in DST, which is created (like `cp -r SRC/. DST`). SRC - reads stdin; DST - writes to stdout (a tar stream for a directory). Files land as user; inside a desktop, two local paths are copied locally.

output.description: nothing, unless DST is - (the file's bytes or a tar stream)

commands.where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: forward
commands.summary: map TCP ports between this machine and the desktop
commands.description: Maps TCP ports both ways until Ctrl-C, over the agent API (no port is opened anywhere else). Each argument is one mapping. PORT or LOCAL:DESKTOP: this machine's 127.0.0.1:LOCAL becomes localhost:DESKTOP in the desktop (a dev server here, reachable by the desktop's browser). -R PORT or -R DESKTOP:LOCAL (reverse; one -R before each such mapping): the desktop's localhost:DESKTOP becomes 127.0.0.1:LOCAL here. Both ends listen on loopback only; the desktop refuses ports below 1024. A port in use on either side fails that mapping, which is retried, and the others carry on. When the connection drops (the desktop stops or restarts, the network blips) it keeps its local listeners, closes open connections and reconnects with backoff (1 s up to 30 s). It exits only on Ctrl-C, or when the token is refused. Run it in the background. Inside a desktop it needs -d too.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: a mapping: PORT or LOCAL:DESKTOP; after -R, PORT or DESKTOP:LOCAL

flags.name: --reverse
flags.description: the next mapping is reverse: a port in the desktop becomes a port here

output.description: one line per mapping each time it goes live: "in LOCAL DESKTOP" or "out DESKTOP 127.0.0.1:LOCAL"; on stderr one line per state change (connected, lost and retrying, port in use)

fields.in: LOCAL DESKTOP: this machine's port, reachable in the desktop at localhost:DESKTOP
fields.out: DESKTOP ADDR: the desktop's port, reachable here at ADDR

commands.where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 after Ctrl-C, 1 when the token is refused (401) or no remote is set up, 2 usage error

commands.name: browser connect
commands.summary: forward the desktop's browser to a local CDP port
commands.description: Listens on 127.0.0.1:PORT and forwards the Chrome DevTools Protocol to the desktop's shared Chromium (the one on its desktop, with the human's logins), so Playwright, Puppeteer or DevTools tools connect as if the browser were local. Prints the URL, then keeps running until Ctrl-C. Run it in the background. Inside a desktop it isn't needed: CDP is at http://127.0.0.1:9221.

output.description: first line: the local CDP URL (http://127.0.0.1:9222); connection log on stderr

commands.where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: remote add
commands.summary: save a desktop as a remote
commands.description: Checks the token against the desktop's agent API and saves the remote in remotes.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deskyard-desktop, default ~/.config/deskyard; mode 0600). URL is the desktop's address, like https://host/alice. Tokens come from the desktop's Agents tab. The first remote becomes the default.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: local name for the remote (letters, digits, . _ -)

examples: deskyard remote add alice https://desktops.example.com/alice --token dyt_…
commands.where: on this machine (no remote needed)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: remote list
commands.description: Lists the saved remotes; * marks the default.

output.description: a table NAME URL TOKEN (token ID only); with --json an array of {name,url,desktop,default}

commands.where: on this machine (no remote needed)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error
